204	## 5. What to actually do, in priority order
205	
206	### 5.1 Fix the recall bias first (cheap, do this before scaling anything)
207	The epoch-3 checkpoint overfits by epoch 4 (§2.4) and, worse, only catches 38/198 real anomalies
208	(§2.4.1). Before spending H100-hours on bigger models, get a clean, less-biased result on the same
209	small model so you have a real comparison baseline. Check the state of the local retrain mentioned
210	in §2.4.1 first — it may already have produced a new checkpoint by the time you read this, in
211	which case re-score it with `scripts/score_predictions.py` before doing anything else:
212	- Since the training set is already 50/50 by construction (§2.1), a plain per-batch balanced
213	  sampler (e.g. `opentslm.time_series_datasets.pamap2.BalancedBatchSampler`, already in the
214	  codebase for PAMAP2, not currently wired into `stage6_esa_cot`) targets mini-batch variance, not
215	  dataset-level imbalance — worth trying, but don't assume it's the dominant fix.
216	- More likely dominant cause: checkpoint selection by validation loss (§2.4.1) rewards fluent
217	  wording over decision accuracy. The more direct fix is checkpointing every epoch (not just the
218	  best-by-loss one) and picking the checkpoint by held-out recall/F1 instead — a change to
219	  `_train_stage`'s checkpoint-selection logic.
220	- Also worth trying regardless: more regularization (lower LR, higher weight decay, dropout in the
221	  encoder) or a lower LoRA rank, since the loss curve alone shows overfitting independent of the
222	  recall issue.
223	
224	### 5.2 Scale the encoder (works for both SP and Flamingo)
225	`model_config.py`'s `EMBED_DIM`/`TRANSFORMER_INPUT_DIM`/`ENCODER_OUTPUT_DIM=128`, `PATCH_SIZE=4`
226	are small. `TransformerCNNEncoder` (`OpenTSLM/src/opentslm/model/encoder/TransformerCNNEncoder.py`)
227	defaults to 6 layers / 8 heads / ff_dim 1024 on top of that. With 8xH100 headroom:
228	- Try a wider embed dim (256–512) and/or more encoder layers/heads — this is the part that
229	  determines how much signal from the raw telemetry survives before reaching the LLM.
230	- These are global constants shared with every other curriculum stage — if you change them,
231	  either accept that stages 1–5 would need retraining too, or fork a stage6-specific encoder
232	  config path instead of mutating the shared defaults blindly.
233	
234	### 5.3 Try OpenTSLMFlamingo with a bigger frozen backbone

236	cross-attention bridge + encoder train:
237	```
238	torchrun --nproc_per_node=8 curriculum_learning.py --model OpenTSLMFlamingo \
239	  --stages stage6_esa_cot --llm_id meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B --gradient_checkpointing
240	```
241	**Caveat, read before doing this**: per `OpenTSLM/README.md`, only `Llama-3.2-1B/3B` and
242	`gemma-3-270m/1b-pt` are "tested and works" — "other variants may work but have not been
243	extensively tested." `OpenTSLMFlamingo.__init__` (`OpenTSLM/src/opentslm/model/llm/OpenTSLMFlamingo.py`)
244	inserts cross-attention layers via `open_flamingo`'s `FlamingoLMMixin`, which depends on the
245	target model's decoder layer naming (`decoder_layers_attr_name`) — this is very likely to need
246	debugging for an untested backbone. Staying within the Llama family (try `Llama-3.1-8B` before
247	jumping to a 70B-class model) reduces that risk. Budget real debugging time for this, and don't
248	let it block the SP-based scale-up in 5.1/5.2, which is much lower risk.
249	
250	### 5.4 Run multiple variants in parallel
251	With 8 GPUs you don't have to serialize experiments. Reasonable split: 1–2 GPUs on the SP
252	regularization fix (5.1), 2 GPUs on encoder scaling (5.2), and the rest on the Flamingo attempt
253	(5.3), so a Flamingo failure doesn't cost you the safer SP improvements.
254	
255	### 5.5 Larger batch size
256	`BATCH_SIZE=4` in `model_config.py` was sized for 32GB. On 80GB H100s (and especially with
257	gradient checkpointing off), push this up via `--batch_size` — larger batches matter here because
258	the paired sampling already balances the 1.8% raw anomaly rate, but more windows per step still
259	means less noisy gradients on a fairly small dataset.
260	
261	## 6. Build the missing baseline (plan's step 7 — genuinely not done)
262	
263	Follow the existing pattern in `OpenTSLM/evaluation/opentslm/` (e.g. `sleep/`, `tsqa/`,
264	`ecg_qa_cot/` each have a `get_*_predictions.py` / `parse_*_data.py` pair) and
265	`OpenTSLM/evaluation/baseline/` (e.g. `evaluate_sleep_cot.py`, `openai_pipeline.py`) to build an
266	ESA-specific baseline: a frozen LLM given the same telemetry window as text-tokenized numbers (no
267	learned encoder), asked the same nominal/anomalous question, to produce a comparison number
268	against OpenTSLM's learned-encoder approach. This is explicitly one of the two things the jury
269	scores (the other being the connector/data-sourcing story), so don't skip it even if a bigger
270	Flamingo run is tempting.
271	
272	## 7. Deliverables to bring back for the demo (plan's step 8)
273	
274	- A trained checkpoint (ideally beating the local `Llama-3.2-3B` + SP run's val loss of ~0.91,
275	  without the epoch-4+ overfitting) plus its `loss_history.txt` and `test_predictions_rank_0.jsonl`.
276	- The baseline comparison number from §6.
277	- 2–3 concrete telemetry windows (plot + ground truth + model's generated rationale) that read
278	  well for a live demo — pull good/bad/borderline examples from `test_predictions_rank_0.jsonl`
279	  style output, not cherry-picked training data.
280	- One clear before/after or SP-vs-Flamingo-vs-baseline comparison figure.
281	
282	## 8. Reference paths
283	
284	| What | Path |
285	|---|---|
286	| TimeNet connector | `TimeNet/packages/timenet-connectors/src/timenet_connectors/datasets/esa/mission1_subsystem5/` |
287	| Compiled registry | `/var/tmp/hrm/zurich-hackathon/timenet_registry/esa/mission1-subsystem5/1.0.0/` |
288	| Raw ESA-AD Mission1 data | `/var/tmp/hrm/zurich-hackathon/data/ESA-Mission1/` |
289	| CoT generation script | `scripts/generate_cot.py`, `scripts/generate_cot_pilot.py` |
290	| Generated CoT labels | `cot_rationales.json`, `cot_rationales_pilot.json` (repo root) |
291	| OpenTSLM dataset loader | `OpenTSLM/src/opentslm/time_series_datasets/esa_mission1/` |
292	| Curriculum entrypoint | `OpenTSLM/curriculum_learning.py` (`--stages stage6_esa_cot`) |
293	| Global model/training config | `OpenTSLM/src/opentslm/model_config.py` |
294	| Checkpoint + logs (being regenerated by a local retrain, §2.4.1) | `OpenTSLM/results/Llama_3_2_3B/OpenTSLMSP/stage6_esa_cot/` |
295	| Baseline eval patterns to copy | `OpenTSLM/evaluation/opentslm/`, `OpenTSLM/evaluation/baseline/` |
296	| Project plan (original framing) | `plan.md` (repo root) |
297	
298	## 9. Time budget
299	
300	This is a 17-hour hackathon window; the pipeline validation above already consumed a chunk of it.
301	Reserve the last 3–4 hours, non-negotiable, for the demo (§7). If the Flamingo/bigger-backbone

303	back to the improved SP run (§5.1/5.2) as the headline result — it's lower-risk and already

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# Sync the parts of the validated local pipeline state that are NOT in git to the 8xH100 cluster.
3	#
4	# The code itself is on GitHub now (branch hackathon-submission of
5	# git@github.com:eklavyagoyal/ehl-zurich-hackathon-submission.git) — clone that on the cluster
6	# first. This script only handles the data tiers .gitignore deliberately excludes: the compiled
7	# TimeF registry (~2MB, always), the trained checkpoint (308MB, opt-in — it's a *.pt file, .gitignore
8	# excludes those), and the raw ESA-AD Mission1 extract (3.6GB, opt-in, only needed to rebuild/widen
9	# the connector's build).
10	#
11	# Usage:
12	#   scripts/sync_to_cluster.sh user@cluster-host [--with-checkpoint] [--with-raw-data] \
13	#       [--remote-root PATH] [--remote-repo PATH]
14	#
15	#   --with-checkpoint   also copy OpenTSLM/results/.../best_model.pt (308MB) — useful as a
16	#                        fallback/reference checkpoint if a bigger cluster run doesn't finish.
17	#   --with-raw-data     also copy the raw ESA-AD Mission1 extract (3.6GB) — only needed if you
18	#                        plan to rebuild/widen the TimeNet connector's build on the cluster.
19	#                        Not needed to just train against the already-compiled registry.
20	#   --remote-root PATH  where data/registry live on the remote, default /var/tmp/$USER/zurich-hackathon
21	#   --remote-repo PATH  where you `git clone`d the repo on the cluster, default
22	#                        ~/ehl-zurich-hackathon-submission (only used for --with-checkpoint, to
23	#                        place best_model.pt at the right path inside your clone)
24	#
25	# After this runs, set on the cluster (see CLUSTER_BRIEF.md §3):
26	#   export ESA_MISSION1_SUBSYSTEM5_REGISTRY=<remote-root>/timenet_registry
27	#   export ESA_MISSION1_SUBSYSTEM5_RATIONALES=<remote-repo>/cot_rationales.json
28	#   export ESA_MISSION1_DIR=<remote-root>/data/ESA-Mission1   # only if --with-raw-data
29	
30	set -euo pipefail
31	
32	if [[ $# -lt 1 ]]; then
33	  echo "Usage: $0 user@cluster-host [--with-checkpoint] [--with-raw-data] [--remote-root PATH] [--remote-repo PATH]" >&2
34	  exit 1
35	fi
36	
37	CLUSTER="$1"
38	shift
39	
40	WITH_CHECKPOINT=false
41	WITH_RAW_DATA=false
42	REMOTE_ROOT="/var/tmp/\$USER/zurich-hackathon"
43	REMOTE_REPO="~/ehl-zurich-hackathon-submission"
44	
45	while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
46	  case "$1" in
47	    --with-checkpoint) WITH_CHECKPOINT=true; shift ;;
48	    --with-raw-data) WITH_RAW_DATA=true; shift ;;
49	    --remote-root) REMOTE_ROOT="$2"; shift 2 ;;
50	    --remote-repo) REMOTE_REPO="$2"; shift 2 ;;
51	    *) echo "Unknown argument: $1" >&2; exit 1 ;;
52	  esac
53	done
54	
55	REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
56	LOCAL_DATA_ROOT="/var/tmp/hrm/zurich-hackathon"
57	
58	echo "==> [1/3] Compiled TimeF registry (~2MB)"
59	ssh "$CLUSTER" "mkdir -p '$REMOTE_ROOT'"
60	rsync -avz \
61	  "$LOCAL_DATA_ROOT/timenet_registry/" "$CLUSTER:$REMOTE_ROOT/timenet_registry/"
62	
63	if $WITH_CHECKPOINT; then
64	  CKPT_REL="OpenTSLM/results/Llama_3_2_3B/OpenTSLMSP/stage6_esa_cot/checkpoints"
65	  if [[ -f "$REPO_ROOT/$CKPT_REL/best_model.pt" ]]; then
66	    echo "==> [2/3] Trained checkpoint (308MB, --with-checkpoint) -> $REMOTE_REPO/$CKPT_REL/"
67	    ssh "$CLUSTER" "mkdir -p '$REMOTE_REPO/$CKPT_REL'"
68	    rsync -avzP "$REPO_ROOT/$CKPT_REL/best_model.pt" "$CLUSTER:$REMOTE_REPO/$CKPT_REL/best_model.pt"
69	  else
70	    echo "==> [2/3] --with-checkpoint given but no checkpoint found at $CKPT_REL/best_model.pt yet (skipping)"
71	  fi
72	else
73	  echo "==> [2/3] Skipping checkpoint (pass --with-checkpoint to include it)"
74	fi
75	
76	if $WITH_RAW_DATA; then
77	  echo "==> [3/3] Raw ESA-AD Mission1 extract (3.6GB, --with-raw-data)"
78	  rsync -avzP "$LOCAL_DATA_ROOT/data/ESA-Mission1/" "$CLUSTER:$REMOTE_ROOT/data/ESA-Mission1/"
79	else
80	  echo "==> [3/3] Skipping raw data (pass --with-raw-data to include it)"
81	fi
82	
83	cat <<EOF
84	
85	Done. On the cluster (after \`git clone --branch hackathon-submission ...\` into $REMOTE_REPO), set:
86	  export ESA_MISSION1_SUBSYSTEM5_REGISTRY=$REMOTE_ROOT/timenet_registry
87	  export ESA_MISSION1_SUBSYSTEM5_RATIONALES=$REMOTE_REPO/cot_rationales.json
88	EOF
89	if $WITH_RAW_DATA; then
90	  echo "  export ESA_MISSION1_DIR=$REMOTE_ROOT/data/ESA-Mission1"
91	fi
92
